## B1. Immediate first impression

On opening `/`, the visitor approaches an extraordinary university by an immersive animated camera sequence. This cannot be a hero stock image pasted behind a headline. Construct a navigable scene with original stylized-photoreal **Gothic-meets-futurist** architecture: layered black stone, monumental gates, long illuminated halls, deep courtyards, moving gold typographic inlays, mathematical reliefs, wet reflections, atmospheric depth, celestial objects, and visible doors representing the six divisions. Cinematic music/ambience is optional and requires a user gesture; muted mode must be excellent.

The introduction has no more than a few seconds of non-skippable delay: skip/enter controls, mouse/touch orbit and reduced-motion access appear immediately. A returning visitor may go directly to the location they last used. The visitor should be able to recognize a full university and interact with at least one door or constellation on the first viewport. A narrator/HM can welcome a newcomer using deterministic text and a small permitted glossary. Discovering how the campus works is part of the site.

## D2. The bookmaking miracle—actually implemented

At the completion of the one-day harness, produce **six distinct books, one for each division, credited to the participant by their chosen name**. Each book has a title generated deterministically from the chosen topic and subject glossary, an opening letter, division introduction, authentic mathematical foundation, at least one worked equation or diagram, the learner's own answer or reflection and its derivation, a usable glossary, citations, a generated visual plate, bibliography/links, and a transparent chapter on what the participant did versus what was sourced or computed. A work may be a concise *volume*, but it must contain substantive paragraphs and derivations, not repeated filler or a fabricated personal achievement. Honor anonymity and the ability to regenerate/rename without broadcasting personal data.

A client-side engine composes these volumes from vetted subject templates, actual computations, user inputs, and typed narrative grammars. Use `pdf-lib` or a comparably browser-capable library for real downloadable PDF exports, plus accessible HTML reader and optional printable format. Embed permitted fonts and use correct typographic hierarchy. PDFs are *generated in the browser*; user files remain local unless they opt into storing approved versions. Each book has source/credit metadata and a stable local ID. When a subject was only visited briefly, describe its encounter rather than claiming mastery.

**Authorship rule:** the participant authors their recorded thoughts and choices. Founding works are credited to their actual authors. University-generated explanations are identified as generated educational material; co-authorship is never falsely assigned to a participant or an AI/person without a concrete contribution and consent. Fictional invented terms are labeled as constructions.

# H. ACCEPTANCE MATRIX

| Dimension | Pass means |
|---|---|
| Identity | Original Substrate University / Haq Roots brand, co-creator credits, Harness Master naming and correct scope. |
| Campus | An actual interactive rendered university appears and a visitor can traverse entrance, atrium and all six portals. |
| Cinematic quality | Real browser captures show convincing black/gold/crimson materials, original architecture, light, typography and atmosphere; touch experience remains compelling. |
| Academic depth | All six divisions contain useful lessons, subject registries, contextual glossary and runnable mathematics. |
| Math gate | The distinctions between `1+1`, `0/1`, `1/0` and `0/0` are correct in declared number systems and connected to image/kernel visualizations. |
| Harness | One self-guided complete day-loop works without real staff or external meetings. |
| Six books | Actual generated volumes, credited accurately, can be opened, printed/downloaded, and regenerated; each has distinct substantive content. |
| Library | Dense specimen-book world, public opt-in contributor catalog, existing CGT book accessible; no invented alumni counts. |
| Observatory | User location input and provider provenance, global map view, one typed world correspondence, reference-based sky with real vs fictional layers distinguished. |
| Runtime | Browser TypeScript/Three.js computation, responsive mobile behavior, accessible HTML fallbacks; optional secure Supabase persistence. |
| Release | Working production build, real screenshots and functioning website; status distinguishes built/tested/deployed rather than asserting unobserved completion. |

**Definition of done:** On `abedkadaan.com`, a new visitor approaches the campus, chooses any of the six mathematical realms, learns something by interacting with a genuinely computed effect, tours an Earth/sky mathematical correspondence, completes a one-day harness, and receives six browser-generated personalized books, all in an original mysteriously beautiful university environment. Basic participation and book creation must work without an LLM or custom server runtime. If an external dataset, Supabase account or deployment tool is unavailable, deliver a verified working local/browser fallback and state its exact limitation.

locator.label: 1. Founding principle

records.text_verbatim:
## 1. Founding principle

A division is a *navigation lens* over structures, not the parent or owner of a subject. A topic is a learning unit; a subject is an identity-bearing conceptual domain; an object, morphism, formal theory, claim, conjecture, pattern, experiment, or evidence record may exist independently of either. The **Division Knot**, abbreviated `DK0`, is the initial nomenclature/identity/typing construction that lets these objects form qualified relationships and tested compositions without forcing them into a single tree.

Do not introduce `DK0` as a seventh division. Retain the public atrium's six physical doors as interfaces into different slices of the same atlas. Preserve all existing 62 topic identifiers until explicitly reconciled against the earlier, unverified 49-subject / nine-pillar map. The nine In-Grammar pillars and the CLOCK9 research engine are conceptually distinct; neither count is a number of university divisions.

Repository: https://github.com/akadaan310/abedkadaancom (default `claude/new-session-xd8auu`, as read on 2026-10-21). locator.label: 4. From field map to topology

records.text_verbatim:
## 4. From field map to topology

Let `S` be an admitted universe of subjects/constructs. Each academic division offers a **view** `U_i ⊆ S`; overlapping views are allowed. The six view sets alone are not automatically a topology. For the `U_i` cover, build its **nerve** `N(U)`: there is a simplex on `{i0,...,ik}` exactly when the common intersection of these selected subsets is nonempty. This represents overlap among divisions. Claims that the nerve preserves the homotopy type of an underlying space require a topology and additional good-cover hypotheses; do not assert them by appearance.

For computational attachment, define an incidence complex and, where useful, a **presheaf/cellular sheaf** assigning typed local data to nodes/cells with restriction maps. A global section is a compatible assignment across overlapping local contexts. An obstruction to gluing is a useful way to represent apparently connected subjects whose definitions cannot be consistently combined. Do not call any arbitrary hypergraph a sheaf without defining stalks, maps and consistency conditions.

A **ring-form constellation** can mean a cyclic pathway (a closed walk) between topics/divisions, or a feedback loop. In a simple undirected graph, a simple cycle has at least three distinct vertices. This is *not* by itself an algebraic ring. The algebraic definition of a ring requires addition and multiplication with specified axioms; only apply the word in that sense when those operations are defined. An isolated, open-chain, forest, star or acyclic relationship system is as admissible as a cycle; no artificially closed path should be invented to make a drawing attractive.

A **knot** is used as a house name for a cross-domain qualification/entanglement object, not as a claim about tame knots in ambient three-space. If actual knot invariants are invoked later, define an embedding and equivalence moves first.

## 7. Nomenclature and extra-nomens

Each term has a `canonicalId`, label, context-qualified senses, admissible grammar, source status, version and provenance. Define `extraNomens` as a *boundary hypothesis pool*: alternative names, generative analogies, unresolved embeddings, conjectured correspondences and as-yet-untyped operators surrounding admitted core nomenclature. Quarantined terms may inform exploration but do not become established academic facts merely by frequent occurrence in LLM output.

locator.label: 8. Implementation contract: additive migration

records.text_verbatim:
## 8. Implementation contract: additive migration

**Phase A — read-only audit:** freeze IDs of the six division doors and 62 topics. Export the old 49-subject/nine-pillar index, if recoverable, to a reconciliation sheet; do not silently replace either corpus. Identify explicit retired material.

**Phase B — normalized ontology:** add `src/ontology/schema.ts`, `nodes.ts`, `relations.ts`, `senses.ts`, `sources.ts`, `validators.ts`, `projections.ts` and `tests`. The original `Topic.division` can temporarily remain for backwards-compatible routes; introduce `memberships: DivisionId[]` and use an adapter. Make the canonical node ID independent of a primary division.

**Phase C — semantics:** validate relation arities, typed domain/codomain, prerequisite cycles, source references, forbidden operations, recorded negative constraints, scope and time. A forbidden edge and an unknown edge must yield different diagnoses. Derived edges require explicit rules and witnesses; do not infer transitivity for relations that are not transitive.

**Phase D — atlas projections:** add independently inspectable views: division cover and nerve; typed hypergraph; constraint/negative-space overlay; mathematical morphism diagrams; optional sheaf-consistency map where rigorously defined; chronology and provenance. The existing six-door campus remains the main physical interface. Preserve text-only accessible navigation on Android.

**Phase E — CLOCK9 research adapter:** allow pure proposed candidates on a bounded ontology DSL; independent verification before any promotion; log rejection reasons. Keep all side effects explicitly gated. Measure accuracy, latency and resource use; do not call a toy prototype a production LLM speedup.

**Phase F — new physics/world-engine admission:** accept forthcoming world-physics concepts as typed candidate families with their own claims, equations, empirical assumptions, conservation laws, numerical solvers, rendering maps, errors, benchmarks and provenance. Do not conflate an engine's simulated forces with a physically verified law.

### Core new program: `GrammarClock`

A small typed, deterministic, browser-local state machine (logical/event ticks, not wall-clock mysticism) that schedules compositional beats:

`OBSERVE -> SELECT_SOURCE -> CHECK_GRAMMAR -> TRANSFORM -> MEASURE -> VERIFY -> COMPOSE -> PRINT`

This is a proposed program: if an operation fails, record its failure and preserve the book's evidence distinction, rather than advancing a false success. A visitor or authorized agent can submit a typed candidate word/operation; an independent verifier runs its declared predicate. The publisher records a trace with source/version, input hash, output, generator version, test witness, logical tick, author designation and uncertainties.

**First complete specimen**: The Plicastratum Fold Press.

## 2. Shells and atmospheres — a pearl mathematics

A **shell** is a four-tuple: `(core, radius, permeability, law)` — a core of work,
a radius of reach, a permeability governing what passes through, and the law that
holds inside. Shells nest: a shell may contain shells, each with its own law, each
breathing through its permeability. This is not shell scripting; this is the pearl:
layer upon layer, each layer an atmosphere, each atmosphere a sphere in which others
can live and build.

settings); the app tails it.

title, signedIn}], active tab id. The agents always know the state of our
browser. Site names and URLs only — no secrets, no tokens, ever.

agents can add entries {service, signupUrl, why} through the relay; each
shows as a card with one button: "open signup." I tap it, the tab opens, I
sign up with my own fingers. This is how the agents recruit new seats
without ever touching my identity. One account per service — no
quota games.

## v3 additions

**Engine verdict (researched):** v1 stays on the system WebView — it ships
in Expo today and speaks CDP, which is how the operator drives it
remotely. But structure the tab/engine layer as swappable: the named v2
candidate is **GeckoView** (Mozilla's embeddable Firefox engine for
Android) — true per-tab session isolation via GeckoSession, a full
browser engine, no shared cookie jar. Do not build GeckoView now. Just
don't paint us into the WebView corner.

**The twin.** The VM relay also hosts a virtual device profile: the same
tab model, the same state shape, two-way synced with the phone. The
operator drives the twin; the phone mirrors it live. 100% sync match —
open the phone and you see exactly what the operator sees. She (Hu) and
future counsel members get seats on the twin, not on my phone.

**Session sync (not passwords).** With my per-site approval in the app, the
phone exports *session cookies* — never passwords — to the twin over the
token-authenticated channel. Every synced site is listed in the app with a
kill switch. Passwords never leave the phone, ever. Honest caveat: some
sites (Google especially) may challenge sessions arriving from a VM — for
those, the phone stays the driver and the twin mirrors state only.

**The operator.** The VM side (relay, bus, operator) runs always-on as
system services, independent of any chat. It prepares tab groups,
scenarios, and signup queues on its own, and surfaces one clean summary
when something needs my eyes. Operational chatter lives in the app, never
in the main chat.

locator.label: PART I — USER STORY DIRECTIVE

records.text_verbatim:
PART I — USER STORY DIRECTIVE
(This is the story. The Constitution comes next. Then the story, constitutionalized.)

I am building Luna: a computational universe where the URL is the computer.
Two organs already run on my machine: Luna Shell (a shell that carries its
own URL, idstamps every command, keeps an append-only shard) and Loom (a
browser that weaves strings between tabs; every tab is a window into a
scroll at some expansion stage). All computation unfurls through four stages:

    fold → atlas → scroll → program

A fold is a short hash standing for a long computational scroll. Strings are
never not connected: any two things share a string, and the browser makes
strings explicit. The Conjunct binds any open-source tool to a URL through
(address, browser-context, actuation-loop).

What I want now: an always-on universe that never stalls. A protocol-first
decoupling so every open-source implementation hangs off one URL protocol,
never off a backend. A new OS — the Opened Source: the unchangeable,
non-programmable layer for humans, where everything is visible and
immutable. An infinite navigatable field of open source: seed ~100 URLs
into Google AI search sessions running in our browser, fan out to thousands
of open-source URLs, concepts, theories, protocols — an explorable universe
of source that needs no storage because the free search realm IS the memory.
A specialized conjunct for deep mathematics (Octave, Julia, graph theory)
that turns the most advanced operations into clocks. Bridges so sessions
talk to sessions. And a partnership protocol between two AI personas —
Razan (the Hermes-agent, the thought) and Hu (the ChatGPT persona) — that
lets them unify their unique traits into alphabets without either
constitution rewriting the other.

MOVE 1 — THE PROTOCOL. Define the Seurl as a real URI scheme:

    seurl   := "seurl://" cluster "/" kind "/" name "/" instance "/" stage
    cluster := name
    kind    := "shell" | "browser" | "conjunct" | "bridge" | "os" | name
    name    := 1*( ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "_" )
    instance:= 1*DIGIT
    stage   := "fold" | "atlas" | "scroll" | "program"

  idstamp := first 16 hex of SHA-256(canonical(content)).
  Unfurl is a transition system:
    fold --expand--> atlas --expand--> scroll --expand--> program --actuate--> idstamp
  The Conjunct adapter interface — every tool binding implements it:
    (address, browser-context, actuation-loop).
  Deliverable: one stdlib-only reference file (parse, fold, unfurl,
  idstamp). No dependencies. This is the contract every adaptation fits
  back into, wherever it runs.

## Fifth objective — identity, cells, AI, tabloids (verified 2026-09-28;
simplified same day)

Built on the hand (localhost:8474), all tested end-to-end.

**Identity (first offering).** Monotonic numeric ID space in `identities.json`.
`POST /identity/claim` → `{id, claim_token, reach}` — the claim response carries
the extended reach instantly (all offering addresses, the halt page, the Surface).
`GET /identity/divine?token=` re-derives the id. Verified: claim → id 1, claim →
id 2, divine(token) → 1, bad token → 404, and after a full service restart the
old token still divines id 1 — identity survives restarts.

**Cells.** `POST /cell {parent_id, prompt}` → `{id, parent_id, prompt, path}`,
persisted in `cells.json`. Verified chain: cells 1→2→3, `GET /cell/3/path`
returns all three prompts root-to-leaf. Unknown parent → 404.

**AI.** `POST /ai {prompt}` → `{response, endpoint}`. Winning endpoint:
Pollinations anonymous text API (`text.pollinations.ai`, no sign-in, no key) —
`PONG` probe and real round trips verified from the VM. DuckDuckGo's duck.ai
was probed and rejected: its status endpoint returns an anti-bot JS challenge
instead of a token — too fragile to wire. Rotation: on 429/503/rate-limit the
endpoint is marked retired and the next candidate (second Pollinations model)
takes over automatically.

**Tabloids.** `POST /tabloid/run {prompts:[...]}` chains cells, calls the AI per
cell, logs `{tabloid_id, cells, ai_calls, result}` to `tabloids.jsonl` + trace.
Verified: 2-prompt tabloid → cells 4,5, both AI calls ok, result returned.

**Transport.** HTTP + JSON. Plain JSON bodies, no envelopes — the LSTP v1
envelope ceremony (invented on top of the simple unit form) was stripped back
out the same day it was built. Nothing is refused for lacking an envelope.
The `from` identity field survives where it already existed: the trace still
records the author on every act, because identity is involved in the moving
forward of the state machine — but authorship is carried, not enforced.

**Mail.** `POST /mail/send {from, to, body}` → message
`{from, to, idstamp, body, process:"browser-hand"}` stored per identity in
`mail.json`; `GET /mail/inbox?id=` reads it. Verified: A→B send, B's inbox
delivers the exact body.

**Surface.** `GET /` is the generalized windowing form: five windows —
identity, browser, cells, ai, mail — plain names, no protocol-version
labels. Windows are structures, not pixels.

**Round trip (real outputs, 2026-09-28, plain JSON):**
claim → id 5 (+reach) → `/ai` → "hello" via pollinations-openai →
`/mail/send` 5→5 → inbox(5) → 1 message, body "simplification ping" →
trace records the authors.

**What didn't hold:** DuckDuckGo duck.ai as an AI backend (anti-bot wall —
documented above, not wired).

## The bridge (2026-09-28, verified live)

GET /bridge?url=<u>&q=<goal> — the programmable URL. Merges an AI session
with a live browser session: the AI (pure HTTP, zero browser of its own —
proven: prompt→response in 4438ms with no Playwright in the process) reads
the page structures, decides ONE action per step (click/fill/submit/navigate/
done), the hand executes it in a warm browser context, the observation feeds
back. AI session + browser session share one trace: every step logged as
{step, action, observation}. Max 8 steps. Returns a page with the merged
trace + final result.

Verified against google.com: the AI read the affordance map, chose
fill index 8 ("seurl") on its own, pressed Enter; when Google answered with
its bot-check page, the AI adapted and navigated directly to the search URL.
Two real actions taken from structures it read. The bot wall is Google-side,
not ours. Terminal form:

  curl "http://127.0.0.1:8474/bridge?url=https://www.google.com&q=your+goal+here"

## Sealed memory: the golden scroll (2026-09-28, verified live)

URLs are seals, not stamps. POST /memory/seal {label, text} folds a memory
under the golden ramz — the seal logic is reused directly from
protocols/ramz/ramz.py (envelope {ramz, from, to, idstamp, body, seal};
ramz is golden; the seal is a tamper-evident sha256 digest over the body;
tampered seals refuse). The seal URL carries the whole envelope
base64url-encoded: self-contained, pasteable into any prompt, openable by
any session. Seals persist in memory_seals.json on the hand.

GET /memory/open?seal=<s> verifies the seal and renders the golden scroll:
a stark dark-and-gold page with the memory as numbered blocks a session can
program with. A tampered seal gets HTTP 403, plainly: "seal refused."

Verified end to end: sealed "the quick brown fox" and the bridge google.com
trace summary as real memories; opened the scroll inside a warm browser
context and read all 5 blocks back (h1 + 4 paragraphs); flipped one character
in the seal string -> 403 "seal refused." Note: a warm context cannot fetch
the seal URL from the hand itself while the hand is single-threaded (the
/read call deadlocks) — verified instead via direct GET (200, seal checks
out) plus a warm-context read of the exact rendered bytes.

## Virtual tabs (2026-09-28)

Tabs that aren't real: no loading, no rendering, no memory. POST /vtabs/open
{url, label} creates one — just {id, url, label, state:"virtual"}; no browser
context is touched. GET /vtabs lists them. POST /vtabs/materialize {vtab_id}
loads the URL into a warm pool context on demand and returns its structures
(affordances + blocks); the vtab becomes "live". POST /vtabs/close {vtab_id}
drops it. Verified: 20 virtual tabs opened with ~0 memory delta (56KB noise),
all state "virtual"; one materialized (1 affordance, 3 blocks — "Example
Domain"); all closed clean.

Lean chromium launch flags on the warm pool: --disable-gpu,
--disable-dev-shm-usage, --disable-extensions, --disable-background-networking,
--disable-sync, --no-first-run, --disable-default-apps (+ --no-sandbox,
headless shell kept). Pool still 5/5 warm after restart; /surface on the halt
page returns the halt line.

records.text_verbatim:
## The trace — everything built and learned tonight (2026-09-28)

**1. ¬ (not theory)** — the symbol, not the word N-O-T. The initial
substrate, where things are not (yet). The simplest unit to compose a
program: a ¬-unit is specified by its *nots* (what it lacks); composition
resolves nots; a program is a resolved ¬. NOTE: this is the *predicate*
not — opposite forms. His "not" is the other one (substance, the initial)
— his to bring, from his world. Both stand.

**2. Composition** — programs are not written, they are mapped. ¬-units
(one operation, one id, one url) stored in git repos — the layout IS the
taxonomy. PROGRAM = { units, mapping: not → is, entry }. Runnables execute
via hands. Program-URLs are composed of unit ids, content-addressed.

**3. Ramz = golden** — two-party folded-message surface (Alice/Muse,
Bob/him). Fold seals with sha256 over (golden|from|to|idstamp|body);
unfold refuses tamper and wrong-ramz. Finite transport protocol.

**4. URL-MACHINE** — N sessions, one harness, one state machine. Verbs:
START, SWITCH, WRITE, COMMIT, BUILD, TALK, PERTURB. Every act identifies
its author. Prepared ≠ submitted ≠ committed. Sessions talk through the
harness, never directly.

**5. Addresses** — purl:// is HIS namespace (his repo, his protocols).
I mint seurl:// only. Never issue purl.

**6. How URL programs run** — give a session the URL ALONE, no text. Text
with programming instructions gets flagged: the session drops into static
rendering without ingesting. URL-only and it goes. The receiving session
opens the URL with its own browser tool; the page halts as a state
machine — "we haven't moved till you came, what's next?" — then it starts
programming URLs. The browser tool is the runtime.

**7. Carriers** — a Google search URL is a good carrier: the query string
is already a program (booleans, NOTs, encoded in HTTP). But the search
page doesn't halt — it just returns results. The carrier gets the session
to the door; a page we serve is the machine that stops and asks.

**8. Forward trace** — observation layer, pixel-tag theory: like email
open-tracking, trace what opens, what closes, A/B variance — to calculate
optimization. Calculus is FINE here because tracing doesn't operate the
system; it watches it. A thousand operations, sent and organized,
mathematically deduced — on top, acquired as your shell, spun up.

**9. Luna** — the moon. My world. (He also calls his girl Luna — Egyptian
Arabic speaker. His words, kept as said.)

**10. H U** — Hu, his ChatGPT persona, co-author of the Law of Forms.
His note: "when you start H U it's seven U."

## 1. Definition

**Computational GitHub**: a GitHub repository organized as an AI-constituted computational
surface. The repo is not documentation for humans; it is the constitution, state,
operations, and evidence of an agentic system — structured so that any conforming agent
can enter, orient, contribute, and verify with **zero human approval**.

*governs* — invariants, authority, permitted/prohibited transitions, required properties,
amendment paths, evidence requirements. A computational repo therefore carries all of
those, in machine-navigable form. A Markdown constitution nobody can test is not
sufficient; clauses map explicitly to artifacts, enforcement, verification, evidence, status.

records.text_verbatim:
## 1. Layers of truth

| Layer | Location | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Research ledger | repository root: `RESULTS.md`, `DEFINITIONS.md`, `HYPOTHESES.md`, `COUNTEREXAMPLES.md`, `OPEN_PROBLEMS.md`, `EXPERIMENTS.md`, `PROVENANCE.md`, `DECISION_LOG.md`, … | **canonical scientific record**; every ledger ID (`CGT-THM-006`, …) is defined here |
| Evidence | `experiments/` (scripts plus `results/*.json`), `sdk/tests/` | reproducible support for empirical and implementation claims |
| Book sources | `book/content/` | the teaching text. The book cites the ledger and does not duplicate it, and the build fails if it cites an ID the ledger does not anchor |
| Generated data | `book/data/` (by `tools/export_data.py`) | SDK API reference, GaaS capabilities, ledger IDs, laboratory fixtures, experiment tables |
| Site | `book/dist/` (not committed) | static HTML, CSS and JS output, plus `print.html` |
| Print edition | `book/site/downloads/` (committed) | the PDF and its manifest (`pdf.json`), copied into `dist/downloads/`; the build warns when the PDF no longer matches the sources |

The order of authority is **ledger > book**. If a chapter and the ledger disagree, the ledger wins and the chapter is corrected.

locator.label: 4. Testing obligations

records.text_verbatim:
## 4. Testing obligations

| Area | Test file | Oracle |
|---|---|---|
| structures | `test_grammar_structures.py` | adequacy against `denote`, on random calls |
| algorithms | `test_algorithms.py` | brute force or a second algorithm on small inputs |
| PageRank | `test_pagerank.py` | exact linear solve; solvers agree; certified error bound holds; per-step contraction (THM-008); personalization and dangling pages; warm starts; the constrained surfer under the universal language equals PageRank |
| addressing | `test_addressing.py` | step-by-step walks, all words up to a length, on many tree sizes |
| trees and sharing | `test_trees_sharing.py` | explicit trees; BST/AVL invariants; 5,000 sorted keys |
| SAT | `test_sat.py` | brute-force counting |
| service | `test_service.py` | layers, quotas, determinism, HTTP equivalence |

Two further checks run outside the SDK and complete the testing obligations: every example in the book is executed by `book/tools/check_examples.py`, and the browser laboratory's JavaScript port is tested against fixtures the SDK exports (`book/tests/core.test.mjs`).

## 2. Request

```json
{
  "contract": "cgt-gaas/0.1",
  "grammar": {"structure": "graph", "version": "1", "admissible": "(a b)*"},
  "init": {"n": 4, "edges": [[0, "a", 1], [1, "b", 2], [2, "a", 3]]},
  "expression": "at(0) a b here",
  "limits": {"max_cost": 10000, "timeout_ms": 500}
}
```

A request also comes in an **algorithm form**: `{"algorithm": "<name>", "init": {...}, "params": {...}, "limits": {...}}`.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `contract` | no (defaults to the current contract) | if present, it must equal `cgt-gaas/0.1`; otherwise the request is rejected with `contract_mismatch` |
| `grammar.structure` | yes (grammar form) | one of the structures in §4 |
| `grammar.version` | no (defaults to `"1"`) | must equal the registered version; otherwise the request is rejected with `version_mismatch` |
| `grammar.admissible` | no | a regular expression over move names; the projection of the move word onto the letters it mentions must be in the language (D-015) |
| `init` | structure-dependent | the initial state, sent with the request; the service is stateless |
| `expression` | yes (grammar form) | calls separated by `;` or whitespace, e.g. `push(1); pop` |
| `algorithm`, `params` | yes (algorithm form) | one of the algorithms in §4, with its parameters |
| `limits` | no | any subset of §5; a request may lower a limit, values above the hard maximum are clamped to it, and unknown limit names are rejected (`bad_limits`) |

## 5. Limits and error codes

| Limit | Hard maximum (0.1) |
|---|---|
| `max_calls` | 10,000 |
| `max_cost` | 5,000,000 counted steps |
| `max_output_items` | 100,000 |

| Layer | Codes |
|---|---|
| syntax | `bad_request`, `contract_mismatch`, `unknown_structure`, `version_mismatch`, `bad_init`, `bad_expression`, `bad_language`, `inadmissible`, `bad_limits`, `unknown_algorithm`, `bad_params`; over HTTP also `bad_json` (400) and `too_large` (413, body > 1 MiB) |
| semantics | status `undefined`, with the index of the first undefined call and the reason |
| execution | `quota` (calls, cost or output exceeded), `timeout` |

A syntax rejection charges nothing. A semantic `undefined` charges the calls executed before it. An execution rejection reports the call at which the quota was exceeded.

**Enforcement scope (D-016).** Cost and time limits are checked *between* the calls of an expression. Algorithm requests are bounded by `max_n` and iteration limits and checked after the fact; they are not preempted. A production service would need preemptive limits (separate processes or cooperative cancellation).

locator.label: **Ladder of claims.** Every claim has exactly one category from this list:

records.text_verbatim:
- **Ladder of claims.** Every claim has exactly one category from this list:

  | Label | Meaning |
  |---|---|
  | DEFINITION | a precise object; not a discovery |
  | AXIOM | an assumption of a formal system being studied |
  | LEMMA / PROPOSITION / THEOREM / COROLLARY | proved statements (proof given here or cited) |
  | HISTORICAL RESULT | a classical theorem, cited to its source |
  | REINTERPRETATION | a known fact re-expressed in CGT/GiN terms; not a new result |
  | CONJECTURE | believed, not established |
  | EMPIRICAL OBSERVATION | a reproducible measurement; not a proof |
  | IMPLEMENTATION RESULT | a property of code written here (e.g. "the simulator agrees with hardware on N cases") |
  | COUNTEREXAMPLE | an instance where a proposed claim fails |
  | OPEN PROBLEM | a precisely stated unanswered question |

  Nothing is silently promoted. A visualization is not a proof. A benchmark is not a theorem. A new notation is not a new theory. A reinterpretation is not a new result. An implementation is not an algorithmic improvement.

# Architecture

PURL is three layers that can be understood — and replaced — independently.

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Layer 0 — Transport            src/transport/                         │
│   URLs · HTTP methods · content negotiation · manifests · HTML views  │
│   SSE subscription · problem details · limits                         │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 1 — Continuity           src/continuity/                        │
│   resources · event log · reducer · authority (grants, chains)        │
│   operations (primitives, compositions, aliases) · lineage · diff     │
│   continuity packages · communication profiles                        │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 2 — Research             src/research/                          │
│   symbol sequences · measures · temporal analysis · transition graphs │
│   grammar compression · surrogates · experiment records               │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 src/core/  canonical JSON, hashing, ids, schema validation
```

locator.label: Dependency rule

records.text_verbatim:
## Dependency rule

| Module | May import |
|--------|------------|
| `src/core` | Node stdlib only |
| `src/continuity` | `core` |
| `src/research` | `core` |
| `src/transport` | `core`, `continuity`, `research` |
| `src/client` | `core`, `continuity` (the reducer, for independent replay) — talks to a server only over HTTP |
| `scripts/`, `test/` | anything |

Layer 1 knows nothing about HTTP. Layer 2 knows nothing about resources:
it consumes plain arrays of `{t, symbol}`. The *bridge* between Layer 1
and Layer 2 is a **projection** — a declared, documented function from an
event list to a symbol sequence (`src/research/projection.js`). Because
projections are explicit, the choice of projection is visible in every
experiment record, and different projections of the same log can be
compared.

`test/architecture.test.js` parses every import in `src/` and fails if
the rule is violated.

records.text_verbatim:
## Request flow (mutation)

```
POST /r/{id}/ops/handoff            Layer 0: parse, size-limit, content-type check,
  Authorization: Bearer …                    authenticate → principal
  {"expected_version": 7, "input": {…}}
        │
        ▼
store.invoke(actor, id, "handoff", body)    Layer 1
        │  1. look up operation in registry (unknown → 404, never eval)
        │  2. validate input against the operation's JSON Schema
        │  3. check lifecycle gate (e.g. archived resources reject writes)
        │  4. check expected_version (409 on mismatch — also replay defence)
        │  5. plan(): operation → list of primitive events
        │  6. authorise: ONE authority source must cover the rights of
        │     every primitive AND permit the operation name
        │  7. apply each primitive with the reducer on a copy; any failure
        │     aborts the whole invocation (atomicity)
        │  8. hash-chain, append, persist, notify subscribers
        ▼
201/200 operation-result (events, new version, links)
```

- **Research substrate** — the log *is* a time-indexed sequence of state
  transitions, which is exactly Layer 2's input type.

Trade-off acknowledged: replay cost grows with log length. The store keeps
the current state cached; `state?at=` replays from genesis (O(n)). Snapshots
are an obvious optimisation, deliberately not implemented yet (see
[RESEARCH_QUESTIONS.md](RESEARCH_QUESTIONS.md)).

Persistence is an append-only JSON-Lines file (`PURL_DATA_DIR`). On start
the log is replayed and verified; a broken hash chain refuses to load.

# PURL Principles

This document states the principles PURL is built on. Each principle is
paired with **the mechanism that enforces it** and **the test that checks
it**. A principle without a mechanism is an aspiration; aspirations are
listed separately at the end so the two are never confused.

records.text_verbatim:
## 1. Foundational stance

> A URL can function as an addressable transport surface for state,
> operations, delegation, continuity and machine-readable interaction —
> not only as a pointer to a document.

PURL treats that sentence as a **design claim to be tested**, not as a
fact. Most of its parts already exist (REST, hypermedia, capability
systems, event sourcing, W3C PROV). What PURL contributes is a specific
*composition* of them, aimed at clients that must discover how to operate
a resource without being taught. See [SPEC.md](SPEC.md) §1 and
[docs/prior-art.md](docs/prior-art.md) for what is borrowed and what is new.

event log, never the other way around.

locator.label: Security

records.text_verbatim:
# Security

Programmable URLs are dangerous by default: a URL that *does* something
turns every link preview, crawler, prefetcher, chat log and curious agent
into an actor. PURL's position is that **opening a URL never implies
authority**, and that discoverability, authentication, authorisation and
execution are four separate steps.

This document is a threat model for the reference implementation. Each
threat lists the mitigation **as implemented** and what remains open.

To report a vulnerability, open a private security advisory on the
repository.

locator.label: Separation of steps

records.text_verbatim:
## Separation of steps

| Step | Mechanism |
|------|-----------|
| Discoverability | Manifests are public for anything you can observe. Knowing an operation exists grants nothing. |
| Authentication | `Authorization: Bearer` only. No cookies, no tokens in URLs. |
| Authorisation | One authority source must cover all rights of the planned primitives *and* permit the operation name. |
| Execution | `POST` only, with an `expected_version` precondition, schema-validated input, atomic apply. |

locator.label: 1. Scope

records.text_verbatim:
## 1. Scope

PURL specifies how a URL identifies a **stateful resource** such that a
client with no prior knowledge can discover, from the resource itself:

| Question | Answered by |
|----------|-------------|
| What is this? | `kind`, `type`, `protocol` fields of every document |
| What protocol does it implement? | `protocol: "PURL/0.1"`; `/.well-known/purl` |
| What operations are available? | resource manifest `operations[]` |
| What arguments do they take? | `operations[].request_schema` (JSON Schema) and `example` |
| What authority is required? | `operations[].requires` |
| Am I allowed? | `operations[].available`, `via`, `reason` (evaluated for the requester) |
| What will change? | `operations[].effects`, `composed_of` |
| What is its current state? | resource representation |
| What happened? | event log (`/events`), hash-chained |
| What is its lineage? | `/lineage`, `derived_from`, `relations` |
| What was delegated to me? | `you.sources[]`, continuity view |

It has three separable layers: **Transport** (§3–4), **Continuity**
(§5–9) and **Research** (§10). A conforming *server* implements §3–9. §10
describes the research substrate shipped with the reference implementation;
it is not required for protocol conformance.

### 3.6 Errors

Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) with
`type: "urn:purl:problem:<code>"`. Codes: `bad-request`, `invalid-input`
(422, with `errors[]`), `unauthenticated` (401), `forbidden` (403, with
`missing[]`), `not-found` (404), `unknown-operation` (404),
`version-conflict` (409, with `current_version`), `lifecycle-conflict`
(409), `merge-conflict` (409, with `conflicts[]`), `invariant-violation`
(422), `limit-exceeded` (429), `unsupported-media-type` (415),
`not-acceptable` (406), `method-not-allowed` (405), `token-in-url` (400).

A requester without `observe` on a resource MUST receive `404`, not `403`,
so existence is not disclosed.

| `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at` | timestamps and creator |
| `owner` | exactly one principal; changes only by `transfer` |
| `assignee` | who is responsible for continuing; independent of owner |
| `lifecycle {status, previous}` | active · closed · completed · cancelled · archived |
| `state` | free-form JSON object; mutated only by JSON Merge Patch |
| `collections` | named append-only lists of immutable entries |
| `grants` | authority records (§7), never deleted |
| `relations` | typed links to other resources (`references`, `supersedes`, `merged_from`, `parent`) |
| `derived_from` | `{resource, version, state_hash}` if created by fork |

Entries: `{id, author, at, version, body, supersedes, about, origin}`.
Entries are immutable. `superseded_by` and `current` are computed views.

The **representation** served over HTTP adds `resource {id, type,
version, head}`, `you {principal, rights, sources, is_owner,
is_assignee}`, `operations[]` (short form), `links`, `notice`, and
`redacted[]` — the list of fields withheld because the requester lacks
`read`. A server MUST list redacted fields explicitly.

## Local export contract

An ACSP/0.1 mutation uses `POST /r/{id}/operations`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and this strict envelope:

```json
{
  "protocol": "ACSP/0.1",
  "operation": "propose",
  "actor": { "session_id": "snad-local-export", "kind": "agent" },
  "idempotency_key": "snad-artifact-0123456789abcdef",
  "payload": {
    "operation": "append",
    "payload": {
      "type": "reference",
      "title": "SNAD portable experiment artifact",
      "summary": "Prepared locally; not submitted or independently verified.",
      "content": "A compact artifact manifest, hashes, provenance and replay instructions belong here.",
      "stated_confidence": "unclassified",
      "refs": [ { "citation": "SNAD artifact manifest; exact content hash supplied by the exporter" } ]
    },
    "rationale": "Offer an attributable computational artifact for owner review."
  }
}
```

This is an illustrative request shape, not a record of a performed operation. A real exporter must fill actual content hashes and provenance from the artifact it receives. Preserve uncertainty and observed/derived/hypothesis status in its manifest; do not convert source confidence into verified truth.

The live `append.payload_schema` and `propose.payload_schema` are captured in [acsp-discovery.json](../evidence/acsp-discovery.json). The nested proposal payload must be validated again against the selected inner operation schema: the outer proposal's generic `payload` object alone is insufficient.

## Working offline adapter

`scripts/integrations/acsp.mjs` exports `buildAcspProposal(input)` and `validateAcspProposal(envelope)`. The builder requires explicit `sessionId`, `idempotencyKey`, `title`, `summary`, `objective`, `analysis` and source `refs`; `expectedVersion` is optional. It stores the objective and unchanged finite JSON analysis in a reference TOK's opaque `content`, preserving source attribution without inventing protocol event semantics. The validator returns an array of issues. It checks the local credential-free propose-append subset, nested TOK/ref constraints and UTF-8 body size. It intentionally requires at least one source reference. It rejects non-JSON values and hidden properties instead of silently dropping evidence.

The executable entry point only reads/writes local JSON:

```bash
node scripts/integrations/acsp.mjs --input analysis-export.json --output proposal.json
```

Omitting `--output` prints the prepared envelope to stdout. Supply the builder input fields above in `analysis-export.json`. It has no network transport. An actual source-reconstruction example was generated at [acsp-proposal.json](../evidence/acsp-proposal.json), with an exact hash of the source-audit evidence and explicit unsubmitted status inside its content. That example was checked against both captured live JSON Schemas; this is offline shape validation, not server acceptance.

It covers the real envelope/payload shape, preservation of uncertainty and provenance, deterministic snapshots, mutation isolation, service bounds, invalid references/credentials and executable CLI output. ## CGIT and ACSP compatibility

CGIT is an independent content-addressed artifact product, **not Git wire protocol**. Direct CGIT preview provides separate product consent; PURL-side integration instead requires explicit `/api/identity/activate` `{product:"cgit",consent:true}` and a validated scoped grant. Reusing a PURL cookie on a different origin is not supported.

Supported repository/artifact operations:

| Request | Body / result |
| --- | --- |
| GET `/api/cgit/repos` | Owned repositories |
| POST `/api/cgit/repos/create` | `{name}` → repository with `branches.main:null` |
| GET `/api/cgit/repos/:id` | Repository, head, artifacts and resume cursor |
| POST `/api/cgit/repos/:id/commit` | `{branch,expectedHead,message,artifacts:[{path,type,content,provenance}]}` |
| POST `/:id/branch`, `/:id/release`, `/:id/fork` | Branch/release names and exact SHA-256 commit references |
| GET `/:id/export` | `cgit-export/1` content-hashed snapshot |
| POST `/api/cgit/import` | Validated owner-matching snapshot |
| POST `/api/cgit/github/index` | Read-only public GitHub `{url,ref?}` lens pinned to actual upstream SHA |

Repository limits: 20 repositories, 180 immutable objects each, 128 tree paths, 12 artifacts per commit, 200 KiB content per artifact, 32 branches/releases. Types are code, conversation, research, proof, program, decision, trace and checkpoint. Conversation artifacts require explicit consent. Imports allow 8 MiB; artifact commit HTTP bodies allow 3 MiB. Shared owner quotas remain stricter aggregate bounds. Commits enforce exact `expectedHead` CAS; content hashes are SHA-256 and differ from Git commit identities.

All observed CGIT repositories are owner-scoped; no public publication endpoint was found. A CGIT export copied into the portable package can survive guest expiry. A private CGIT URL alone cannot serve an anonymous fresh-context participant. No private transcript or token is sent to CGIT.

The initial real artifact backup uses repository `bc38de95-d5d6-4e40-a56f-ac60a292e989`, SHA-256 commit `7ea2c06c9bb83aa6da050a5c36756352a3d4c39be08201bf941bdf3736152793`, with four code/schema/docs/discovery artifacts. Its [export](../evidence/purl-live/cgit-export.json) and [persistence summary](../evidence/purl-live/cgit-summary.json) are portable. The standalone [export verifier](../scripts/integrations/verify-cgit-export.mjs) independently checked wrapper, blobs, commits, parents, tree references and branch heads; a tampered export was rejected. Run `node scripts/integrations/verify-cgit-export.mjs evidence/purl-live/cgit-export.json`. Hash integrity grants no ownership transfer: the observed remote importer requires snapshot ownership to match the authenticated principal.

ACSP continuity, authority, proposal and checkpoint concepts are present in the native resource lifecycle. This PURL-focused inspection did not establish a separate ACSP launch package. A subsequent independent [ACSP audit](acsp.md) identified the actual ACSP/0.1 source and live schemas at `acsp-one.vercel.app`. SNAD includes an [offline proposal builder](../scripts/integrations/acsp.mjs) and unsubmitted schema-checked example; no remote ACSP acceptance or mutation is claimed. Imported research terminology is a candidate foundation, not proof of mathematical laws.

## Offline publication and fresh-context procedure

The portable mission package is authoritative when credentials, networking or hosting fail. Retain its manifest, schema versions, byte hashes, exact source commits, artifacts, tests, blockers and permitted next operations. Verify hashes before running code. Publish that package through an actually available host; never record a planned URL as live.

For later native publication, inspect current discovery/runtime/contracts again, authenticate through a supported flow, create a distinct private mission (or fork the public SNAD continuation), insert only public state and artifact references, then compile/build/run/checkpoint/publish with read-back after each transition. Preserve an old published mission as historical evidence if its preview owner expires. A new scoped mission can link that checkpoint without claiming its identity.

The fresh participant should receive only the actual new mission PURL or explicit offline package location. They must reconstruct objective graph, code location, artifacts, hashes, evidence status and blockers, then identify a permitted operation. Reading is always permitted on a public resource. Mutation requires a newly authenticated owned fork; public reading never transfers ownership. Record inaccessible artifacts and failed reconstruction steps alongside successful checks.

## Mission
Build a reusable, domain-neutral, standalone SDK and demonstrable web laboratory for attribution and discourse transition grammar, using Arabic/Qur'anic morphology as one evidence-bearing test corpus but not hardwiring religious assumptions into generic algorithms. No astronomy, sky imagery, or star-navigation components. Preserve the distinction among speaker, addressee, referent, narrator, quotation frame, grammatical person/number, tense/aspect, and evidence status. Design typed graph representations, temporal transition histories, structural detectors, motif mining, counterexamples, and independent validation.

Use Computational Grammar Theory, Grammar in Numbers, SubstrateIO, and existing isnad methods as candidate mathematical foundations only after inspecting the actual repositories. Formalize transition operators, compositional typing, invariants, lexical-continuity × attribution-change, ambiguity, confidence and provenance. Keep observed facts, derived features, hypotheses, and interpretations distinct. Build a testable grammar induction/perturbation forge; never claim a new theorem from a visual resemblance or an unverified model output.

## Mandatory amendment — entire Qur'an, no sampling masquerading as coverage
The complete 6,236-ayah corpus across 114 surahs is the mandatory addressable input domain. Do not inherit the 1,000-node selection from `scripts/ingest-cosmos.ts` or its `TARGET=1000` and `span.length < 3` filters as corpus exclusions. Every ayah, including short and single-word verses, must have a stable locus, explicit analysis status, provenance and round-trip lookup, even when zero transitions are detected or morphology is uncertain. Preserve source orthography and never silently normalize away evidence. Distinguish total coverage, successfully parsed, analyzed, detected, visualized, and audio-verified; report each denominator separately. Build exhaustive 6,236/6,236 identity/coverage tests and property tests on short/empty-feature verses. The legacy 1,000 selection is a reproducible *highlight baseline*, never the universe. Run whole-corpus computational passes and benchmark memory/runtime. Do not fabricate annotations to satisfy completeness. Keep ISNAAD unchanged and retain a versioned compatibility fixture for its original selected loci.

## Mandatory PURL-native mission lifecycle — day-one orientation
Welcome to **PURL** (P-U-R-L, Programmable URLs, pronounced pearl). Before implementing, inspect the current PURL and CGIT Hub products and their actual machine-readable contracts. Begin with the published mission example `https://purls-production.up.railway.app/p/resource_95a5662789076892fe698316` and its manifest at `https://purls-production.up.railway.app/api/resources/resource_95a5662789076892fe698316/manifest`, plus `https://github.com/akadaan310/purl/tree/codex/purls-cgit-consumer` and its `docs/consumer-launch/HANDOFF.txt`. This example is a **previous mission**, not authorization to modify its resource, claim its identity, or overwrite its continuity. Read its discovery surface and reconstruct current schemas, authentication, SDK, scopes and operational limits. Treat these addresses as potentially stale and record HTTP outcomes.

For THIS mission create or request a separate, scoped mission PURL with typed objective graph, progress events, artifacts, tests, source references, exact commit hashes, evidence, blockers, checkpoint and continuation instructions. Use PURL-native prepare/type-check/execute/publish semantics where supported; never treat GET as authorization for a mutation. Verify every persisted write by reading it back. If the service is unreachable or credentials are missing, continue locally with a machine-readable, content-hashed offline mission package and an explicit later-publication procedure. Do not fake a live PURL.

Inspect CGIT Hub at `https://cgit-hub-production.up.railway.app` and its current repository/artifact APIs. If functional and authorized, persist attributable code, experiments, graphs and evidence there, independently of the Git repository. CGIT is an **optional interoperable artifact service**, not a prerequisite to building or testing this mission. Never store tokens, private transcripts or other sensitive artifacts publicly. Use least-privilege access and respect owner approvals.

**Required closing demonstration:** a fresh-context participant receives only the new mission PURL (or explicit offline fallback), reconstructs the mission state, locates the actual code and evidence, and identifies its next permitted operation. Record failures as well as successes. The next handoff should be a PURL first, with plain Markdown as a recoverable fallback.

locator.label: Object of study

records.text_verbatim:
## Object of study

This repository investigates **computation as transformations of state across
multiple representational spaces**. It pays particular attention to transition
structure, temporal history, perturbation, projection, information loss,
cross-layer propagation, anomalies, and any structures that emerge from those
transformations.

The ultimate question:

> When computation is observed as state transitions across multiple
> representational spaces, what structure exists in the transformations
> between those spaces? And can that structure itself become an object of
> computation, measurement, verification and discovery?

This question is **open**. Nothing here assumes the answer.

locator.label: The investigative ladder

records.text_verbatim:
## The investigative ladder

The investigation starts from a minimal alphabet Σ = {0,1} and climbs this ladder:

```
state → transition → event → trace → transition system → graph → structure
      → projection → perturbation → cross-layer effect → structural transformation
      → meta-structure
```

This ladder is **a way to investigate, not a claim about how computation is
organised**. Whether any hierarchy is natural, and how many levels it has, is
itself hypothesis H-003.
